assignments.reason: Eretz Yisrael is the place where emunah, tefilla, and nisim are rooted ('עִקַּר אֱמוּנָה... אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּאֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל'). Its essential nature in this Torah is as the geographic locus of faith and prayer — it is the holy land dimension of the emunah domain, not a separate thematic cluster.

Geulah (redemption) is the ultimate telos of emunah in this Torah. The text says 'עִקַּר הַגְּאֻלָּה תָּלוּי בָּזֶה' — it depends entirely on emunah. Its essential nature is the culmination of faith: the supra-natural restoration that is the endpoint of the emunah-tefilla-nisim chain. It belongs in the faith domain as the goal of faith.

The 'joining of emet and emunah' is the union of the masculine and feminine dimensions of faith. Its essential nature is the completion of emunah — emunah is only fully realized when emet joins it ('אֱמוּנָה אִתְקְרִיאַת כַּד אִתְחַבַּר בַּהּ אֱמֶת'). This is structurally an emunah concept — the moment faith becomes complete.
This is a variant expression of geulah — 'the redemption depends on this.' Same essential nature as גאולה: the culmination of emunah. It is the faith-domain's telos expressed as a dependent clause.

In this Torah, 'ish v'isha' is explicitly the union of emet and emunah — 'אִישׁ וְאִשָּׁה הֵם בְּחִינַת הִתְחַבְּרוּת אֱמֶת וֶאֱמוּנָה'. The individual nodes איש and אשה are already in Package 1. This combined node represents the same emunah-emet pair that is the heart of the Torah's conclusion.

This node describes the blemishing (pegam) of emunah, tefilla, and Eretz Yisrael. Its essential nature is the emunah domain in its damaged state — the three core concepts of Package 1 are named explicitly. The damage is to faith itself, so the node belongs to the faith package.

The 'lack of emunah' is structurally a state of emunah — it is the absence of faith, not a separate domain. The Torah opens with this: 'עִקַּר הַגָּלוּת אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל חֶסְרוֹן אֱמוּנָה'. Its essential nature is emunah in deficit.

assignments.node_id: כשפגם אברהם "במה אדע" (שם ט"ו), ובזה פגם בירשת ארץ
assignments.node_text: כְּשֶׁפָּגַם אַבְרָהָם "בַּמָּה אֵדַע", וּבָזֶה פָּגַם בִּירֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ
assignments.reason: Avraham's blemish of 'bamah eida' is a failure of emunah — he questioned God's promise about inheriting the land, which is equated with emunah and tefilla in this Torah. His essential nature here is as the paradigm of a lapse in faith, placing him in the emunah domain.

assignments.node_id: כי יש בני־אדם המכסים כלליות הנסים, הכלולים במלאך דפריטא שפותה, מכסים בדרך הטבע. וכשתכלה זאת ותתרבה אמונה בעולם
assignments.node_text: כִּי יֵשׁ בְּנֵי־אָדָם הַמְכַסִּים כְּלָלִיּוּת הַנִּסִּים... וּכְשֶׁתִּכְלֶה זֹאת וְתִתְרַבֶּה אֱמוּנָה בָּעוֹלָם
assignments.reason: This node describes the covering of miracles with naturalistic explanations — the very activity of the anti-emunah force. The text identifies these people as those who 'cover' (מכסים) the nisim — which is the function of shikcha/mas (forgetting/covering over the miraculous). Their essential nature is the evil counter-force to emunah, which is Package 5.

assignments.node_id: יכלו האפיקורסים שאין להם אמונה בנסים, ומכסים כל הנסים בדרך הטבע
assignments.node_text: שֶׁיִּכְלוּ הָאֶפִּיקוֹרְסִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אֱמוּנָה בְּנִסִּים, וּמְכַסִּים כָּל הַנִּסִּים בְּדֶרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע
assignments.reason: The apikorsim are the human agents of the shikcha force — those who lack emunah in nisim and cover miracles with nature. The additions file explicitly notes them as the 'face' of forgetting/naturalism. Their essential nature is the anti-emunah force of Package 5.

connected_to: כי יש בני־אדם המכסים כלליות הנסים, הכלולים במלאך דפריטא שפותה, מכסים בדרך הטבע. וכשתכלה זאת ותתרבה אמונה בעולם
יכלו האפיקורסים שאין להם אמונה בנסים, ומכסים כל הנסים בדרך הטבע
assignments.reason: Mashiach is the ultimate expression of geulah, which this Torah places squarely in the emunah domain. 'אָז יָבוֹא מָשִׁיחַ' — when emunah spreads in the world. Mashiach's essential nature here is the culmination of the emunah-tefilla-geulah chain, not a separate domain.

Galut (exile) is the consequence of lacking emunah. Its essential nature in this Torah is the anti-emunah state — the condition that results from the shikcha/naturalism force. The Torah opens by saying 'עִקַּר הַגָּלוּת אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל חֶסְרוֹן אֱמוּנָה'. Galut is the evil domain's condition, the mirror of geulah.

connected_to: כשפגם אברהם "במה אדע" (שם ט"ו), ובזה פגם בירשת ארץ
assignments.reason: Galut Mitzrayim is the paradigmatic exile — the text says 'מִצְרַיִם הוּא הֶפֶךְ הַנִּסִּים'. Egypt is the opposite of nisim, the opposite of emunah. Its essential nature is the anti-emunah domain: the place where there is no prayer, no miracles. Same evil polarity as galut generally.

assignments.package_label_en: Counsel and Marriage — the Holy Side
assignments.reason: Atzat ha-tzaddikim is counsel from the righteous — the core concept of Package 3. The node עצה is already in Package 3; atzat ha-tzaddikim is its active, personified form. Its essential nature is holy counsel, the dominant theme of Package 3.

assignments.package_label_en: Counsel and Marriage — the Holy Side
assignments.reason: This is a variant spelling of עצת הצדיקים — counsel of the righteous. Same essential nature: holy counsel. Belongs in Package 3 (Counsel and Marriage). It produces emet, but it IS counsel.

assignments.package_label_en: Counsel and Marriage — the Holy Side
assignments.reason: Drawing close to tzaddikim and following their counsel is the practical expression of receiving holy eitza. Its essential nature is the process of receiving counsel — the relational act that Package 3 describes. The node העצות שמקבל מהם is already in Package 3.

assignments.node_id: התקרבות לצדיקים וילך בדרך עצתם; ועל־ידי שמקבל מהם עצתם
assignments.node_text: הִתְקָרְבוּת לְצַדִּיקִים וְיֵלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ עֲצָתָם; וְעַל־יְדֵי שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל מֵהֶם עֲצָתָם
assignments.package_label_en: Counsel and Marriage — the Holy Side
assignments.reason: Extended variant of the previous node — approaching tzaddikim and receiving their counsel. Same essential nature: the act of receiving holy eitza. Package 3.

assignments.node_id: הוא מקבל טפי השכל של הצדיק
assignments.node_text: הוּא מְקַבֵּל טִפֵּי הַשֵּׂכֶל שֶׁל הַצַּדִּיק
assignments.package_label_en: Counsel and Marriage — the Holy Side
assignments.reason: Receiving the intellectual drops (tipei ha-sekhel) of the tzaddik is the metaphysical mechanism of counsel-as-marriage. The tipot/drops are the 'seed of emet' transmitted through eitza. The nodes תלת טפין and תלת מחין are already in Package 3. This is the same counsel-seed-intellect structure.

assignments.node_text: הוּא מְקַבֵּל טִפֵּי הַשֵּׂכֶל שֶׁל הַצַּדִּיק
assignments.package_label_en: Counsel and Marriage — the Holy Side
assignments.reason: Variant node_id of the same concept as above — receiving the tzaddik's intellectual drops through counsel. Same essential nature: the counsel-marriage mechanism. Package 3.

Arriving at emet (truth) is the outcome node. Emet is already in Package 1 (it was merged in as the masculine partner of emunah). 'לָבוֹא לֶאֱמֶת' is the attainment of emet — same domain as אמת itself.

connected_to: התקרבות לצדיקים וילך בדרך עצתם; ועל־ידי שמקבל מהם עצתם
assignments.reason: The engraving of emet in the person is the result of receiving counsel. Its essential nature is emet — truth being inscribed. Emet is in Package 1. This is emet's actualization, not counsel itself.

assignments.node_id: יכול לקבל העצות מצדיק, שהוא כלה זרע אמת
assignments.node_text: וְיָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל הָעֵצוֹת מִצַּדִּיק, שֶׁהוּא כֻּלֹּה זֶרַע אֱמֶת
assignments.package_label_en: Counsel and Marriage — the Holy Side
assignments.reason: The ability to receive counsel from the tzaddik, which is 'all seed of emet' — this is the reception of holy counsel. Its essential nature is the counsel domain: it describes the capacity to receive eitza, which is the core of Package 3.

connected_to: האדם נצול מעצת הנחש, מנשואין של רשע, מבחינת נאוף
assignments.reason: Mitzvat tzitzit is the practical commandment form of ציצית, which is already in Package 2. Its essential nature is the same: shmirat ha-brit through the garment. It is tzitzit.

connected_to: זכה לבן פרת, שנשמר מנשואין של נחש, מזווג של הסטרא־אחרא
assignments.reason: A variant expression of ציצית ('because of tzitzit'). Its essential nature is tzitzit — the guardian of the brit. Package 2.
Guarding the tzitzit is the active-practice form of ציצית. Its essential nature is the tzitzit/shmirat-ha-brit domain of Package 2.

The text explicitly says 'הַשִּׂמְלָה הַיְנוּ צִיצִית' — the garment IS tzitzit. This is definitionally ציצית. Package 2. (The additions file also notes this edge could be reclassified as bechina since 'הַיְנוּ' is definitional language.)

connected_to: יכול לקבל העצות מצדיק, שהוא כלה זרע אמת
assignments.reason: The eyes are the site of the niuf temptation ('עִקַּר הַנִּאוּף תָּלוּי בָּעֵינַיִם'). Tzitzit is identified as 'bchinat einayim' — the protection of the eyes. The eyes are a neutral body part that in this Torah functions as the battleground of shmirat ha-brit. They belong with Package 2 (Yosef/Tzitzit) as the organ that tzitzit guards.
Gazing at the tzitzit is a practice centered on tzitzit. Its essential nature is tzitzit — it is the act of engaging with the tzitzit garment. Package 2.

The remedy for the sick person through gazing at tzitzit is a practical outcome of the tzitzit domain. It is a segulah tied to tzitzit; its essential nature is the healing power of the brit-guarding garment. Package 2.

assignments.node_id: האדם נצול מעצת הנחש, מנשואין של רשע, מבחינת נאוף
assignments.node_text: הָאָדָם נִצּוֹל מֵעֲצַת הַנָּחָשׁ, מִנִּשּׂוּאִין שֶׁל רָשָׁע, מִבְּחִינַת נִאוּף
assignments.reason: This node describes being saved FROM the serpent's counsel, evil marriage, and niuf. The things being saved from — atzat ha-nachash, nisuin shel rasha, niuf — are all Package 4 concepts. The node's essential content describes the evil domain (what one is rescued from), making it a Package 4 concept in its descriptive nature.

Protection from niuf is the protective function of tzitzit/shmirat ha-brit. Its essential nature is guarding — the active defense that tzitzit provides. It IS the function of Package 2. Though it mentions niuf (Package 4), the concept itself is the protective shield, which belongs to the guardian domain.
Protection from the serpent's counsel is the core function of tzitzit in this Torah. Same reasoning as שמירה מנאוף — this is the guarding role of the tzitzit/brit domain. Package 2.
Extended form of the previous protection node — guarding from the serpent's counsel and its pollution. Same essential nature: the protective function of tzitzit. Package 2.

assignments.package_label_en: Counsel and Marriage — the Holy Side
assignments.reason: Holy union (zivuga di-kedusha) is the marriage/union concept in its holy form. Package 3 already contains נשואין and זווג. Zivuga di-kedusha is the same essential nature — holy marriage/union. Though tzitzit enables it, its essential nature IS union.

assignments.node_id: זכה לבן פרת, שנשמר מנשואין של נחש, מזווג של הסטרא־אחרא
assignments.node_text: זָכָה לְבֵן פֹּרָת, שֶׁנִּשְׁמַר מִנִּשּׂוּאִין שֶׁל נָחָשׁ, מִזִּוּוּג שֶׁל הַסִּטְרָא־אָחֳרָא
assignments.reason: Ben Porat (Yosef) who was guarded from evil marriage — this describes Yosef's merit of shmirat ha-brit. 'Ben Porat' is the Yosef archetype. Its essential nature is Yosef/shmirat ha-brit. Package 2.

connected_to: שעל־ידיהם אין יכולים לקבל עצת צדיקים, זרע אמת
assignments.reason: The counsel of the serpent and the wicked is the core concept of Package 4. The node עצות הנחש is already in Package 4. This is the same essential nature: evil counsel.

assignments.node_id: שעל־ידיהם אין יכולים לקבל עצת צדיקים, זרע אמת
assignments.node_text: שֶׁעַל־יְדֵיהֶם אֵין יְכוֹלִים לְקַבֵּל עֲצַת צַדִּיקִים, זֶרַע אֱמֶת
assignments.reason: The inability to receive holy counsel due to evil counsel is the consequence of the serpent's counsel — structurally it is the blocking function of evil eitza. Its essential nature is the evil-counsel domain: it describes what evil counsel does (prevents reception of holy counsel). Package 4.
